reference.source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology / palliative care guidelines
clinicalPearls: Sarcopenia is the progressive, generalised loss of skeletal muscle mass together with reduced muscle strength or physical performance
Current definitions emphasise low muscle strength as the primary criterion, with low muscle mass confirming the diagnosis and poor performance marking severity
Grip strength and gait speed are simple, validated bedside measures that flag probable sarcopenia
The SARC-F questionnaire is a quick screening tool for case finding in clinical practice
Sarcopenia can be primary (age-related) or secondary to disease, inactivity, or undernutrition, and it overlaps with but is distinct from frailty and cachexia
It is a major contributor to falls, disability, loss of independence, and adverse surgical and hospital outcomes
Progressive resistance exercise is the most effective intervention and is more powerful than nutrition alone
Adequate protein and total energy intake, correction of vitamin D deficiency, and treatment of underlying conditions support muscle maintenance
reference.pathophysiology: Sarcopenia results from an imbalance between muscle protein synthesis and breakdown, driven by ageing changes including loss of motor neurons and motor units, reduced anabolic hormone levels, anabolic resistance to dietary protein, mitochondrial dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and physical inactivity. Type II (fast-twitch) fibres are preferentially lost, and fatty and fibrous infiltration of muscle further reduces quality and strength. The result is diminished force generation and impaired physical performance out of proportion to the loss of mass alone.
additionalDifferentials: Cancer cachexia with inflammation-driven muscle wasting
Frailty syndrome (overlapping but broader multisystem construct)
Disuse atrophy from immobility or prolonged bed rest
Neuromuscular disorders such as motor neuron disease or myopathy
Endocrine causes including hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, and hypercortisolism
additionalInvestigations: Muscle strength testing, particularly handgrip dynamometry
Assessment of muscle mass using DXA or bioimpedance where available
Physical performance measures such as gait speed, the short physical performance battery, or timed up-and-go
Laboratory evaluation for reversible secondary causes including vitamin D, thyroid function, and inflammatory markers
redFlags: Rapid muscle loss suggesting underlying malignancy or cachexia rather than age-related decline
Recurrent or injurious falls resulting from profound weakness
Neurological features pointing to a primary neuromuscular disorder
reference.prognosis: Sarcopenia predicts falls, fractures, functional decline, hospitalisation, and mortality, and it worsens outcomes across surgery and acute illness. It is at least partly reversible: resistance training combined with adequate protein intake can improve strength and performance, and earlier intervention yields better results.
pitfalls: Attributing weakness solely to old age and not screening or intervening
Relying on nutritional supplementation without prescribing resistance exercise
Overlooking secondary and reversible causes such as vitamin D deficiency and endocrine disorders
Missing the overlap with frailty and cachexia and thereby underestimating overall risk
management: Prescribe progressive resistance and strength training as the cornerstone intervention to improve muscle strength and physical performance
Ensure adequate dietary protein intake distributed across meals, with oral nutritional supplementation where intake is insufficient
Correct vitamin D deficiency and optimise overall nutrition with dietitian input
Identify and treat reversible secondary causes such as endocrine disorders, inactivity, and undernutrition, and review contributory medications
Implement multidisciplinary falls prevention and functional rehabilitation through physiotherapy and comprehensive geriatric assessment
Monitor response and progression with bedside measures such as handgrip strength and gait speed
